jobs.description: Employer: GoSkyHy Expires: 10/03/2026 GoSkyHy Community & Traveler Experience InternWhere Adventures Begin — and where every traveler feels like they've found theirpeople.Location: Remote + your campus | Commitment: ~10 hrs/week, one semester |Compensation: $1,337/month flat — same in every country (≈$30+/hour at ~10hrs/week) + performance bonuses | Academic credit: Supported — arranged byyou through your university; we'll complete any employer paperworkWho We AreGoSkyHy is the social travel platform where people connect, create groups, andbook unique adventures around the world. We help people find hidden gems, jointravel crews, and turn "someday" trips into this-weekend plans. An app can getsomeone to download — but community is what makes them stay. That's yourdepartment.The GigYou'll be the heartbeat of the GoSkyHy community — the reason new users feelwelcomed instead of lost.Bring the community to life. Seed and moderate travel groups, welcome newmembers, spark conversations, and connect travelers who should obviously be onthe same trip. You set the vibe of the platform.Grow our host network. Find and recruit the people running amazing local events— hikes, food tours, hidden-gem adventures — and help them get set up asGoSkyHy hosts.Be the voice of the traveler. Talk to users, gather feedback, spot the frictionpoints, and bring it all to the founding team. Your insights will directly shape theproduct — yes, the team will actually read them.You Might Be Our Person If...You're the friend who makes sure nobody eats lunch alone. You reply to groupchats first and remember everyone's name at the party. You're studyinghospitality, psychology, communications, business — or none of the above,because warmth and hustle beat any major. Bonus points if you've ever run a club,moderated a Discord, or planned a trip for more than four people without agroup falling apart.The Pay$1,337 every month. Yes, really. A flat monthly rate, the same whether you're inTexas, London, Sydney, or Singapore — at roughly 10 hours a week, that's over$30/hour. For context: the average US marketing internship pays $17.66/hour. Wepay elite rates because we expect elite work.Community bonuses. We set milestones together — active travel groups, hostsonboarded, insights shipped — and hitting them earns cash bonuses on top ofyour monthly rate.A raise for coming back. Crush your first semester and get invited for a second?Your monthly rate goes up.Paid monthly, on time, every time. Real payments, real records — this is a job, nota favor.Based on approximately 10 hours per week. Hours are agreed and tracked so youreffective hourly rate always exceeds your local minimum wage.What You Get (a.k.a. Why This Beats a Boring Internship)Real product influence. Your user research and feedback reports go straight tothe founders. "That feature exists because of my insight" is a rare thing to say asan intern anywhere.A community you built. The travel groups you seed, the hosts you recruit, theusers you welcome — that's a measurable, portfolio-ready story about growingand running a real community.Direct access to founders. Weekly sessions with the GoSkyHy team — no middlemanagers, no busywork. You'll learn community-building, user research, andproduct thinking from the inside.Academic credit. Want course credit on top of the paycheck? It's yourresponsibility to arrange it with your university — every school's process isdifferent — but once you do, we'll gladly complete any employer paperwork,evaluations, or supervisor sign-offs your program requires.A recommendation letter from the CEO. Crush it, and you'll have a personalizedletter — and a reference who picks up the phone when recruiters call.A title that works for you. "Community & Traveler Experience Intern, GoSkyHy" onyour LinkedIn and resume from day one.First shot at paid roles. As GoSkyHy grows, our intern alumni are first in line.The Fine PrintThis is a part-time, paid internship designed around your learning: you'll set goalswith us, get mentorship and feedback, and build a portfolio — all on a schedulethat flexes around exams. One semester, with the option to continue.How to ApplySkip the cover letter. Send us:1. Your resume2. A few sentences on the best adventure you've ever had3. A community you've been part of (or built) and what made it work4. One idea for making new GoSkyHy users feel instantly at homeEmail: partners@goskyhy.com | www.goskyhy.com

You must have excellent communication skills, demonstrate creativity, be detail-oriented, be comfortable working on deadlines and operate and dress professionally. You also must be comfortable asking questions, being proactive and learning by doing.AccountabilitiesBefore applying, ensure this is the right seat for you on our team. Bring big ideasReal impact begins when we reimagine what’s possible. Big ideas spark energy, drive, sustainable growth, and create bold solutions that serve our clients and our communities. Catalyze resultsWe measure success by the trust we build and the positive change we create. As a B Corporation, we hold ourselves accountable to outcomes that advance people, planet, prosperity, and purpose in every engagement. Do it togetherSustainable impact isn’t achieved alone. We value and activate the diverse skills, perspectives and lived experiences of our team and partners. By aligning around shared goals - we turn collective effort into transformative change.Job QualificationsRequired experience and core competencies for this position include: Applicants must have strong written and verbal communication skillsApplicants must be a college junior or seniorApplicants who have completed communications coursework are preferredApplicants should be proficient in Google Docs and Sheets (or MS Office equivalent)Applicants should be a master of AP Style and be able to apply it within PR tacticsApplicants must be available to work between hours of 8:30 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. CT (flexible)Applicants must have their own laptop, access to strong internet connection and transportation Kane Communications is an equal-opportunity employer. jobs.description: Employer: Confluence Environmental Center, AmeriCorps Program Expires: 10/07/2026 Dates of Service October 21st, 2026 – July 29th, 2027 (1,200 hours, approx. 32 hours/week) POSITION TITLEDepave for Trees Coordinator Project PARTNEROregon Walks and Depavehttps://oregonwalks.org/https://www.depave.org/ Position SummaryThis position is in partnership between the Confluence Environmental Center, AmeriCorps Program, DePave and Oregon Walks. 82nd Avenue is in the middle of major public reinvestment, and one of the clearest calls from the community has been for less pavement and more green space, especially trees. This position exists to answer that call on the ground: designing a new "micro-depaving" pilot program that partners directly with private landowners to remove small sections of pavement, plant a tree, and support the landowner in maintaining it. This position will build the relationships and evidence base for a micro-depaving program model through community outreach, education, and partnership building to support increased access to greenspaces along 82nd Avenue.Estimated time breakdown: 40% research, pilot program design; 30% outreach, recruitment, and education; up to 10% project fundraising; and 20% Confluence cohort/leadership development activities. Essential Functions (to include, but not limited to):Research and design a "micro-depaving" program model for small-scale private-lot depaving projects along the 82nd Avenue corridor including explanations on how to identify sites, how to engage with land owners, how to navigate permitting, and how to contract with partners.Outreach to private landowners along 82nd Avenue to identify potential participantsBuild and maintain relationships with community and technical partners, including the 82nd Avenue Coalition, BRANCH Coalition partners, the City of Portland, and local workforce development organizations.Coordinate with City of Portland permitting staff to understand how the program design stays within permit-exempt thresholds.Identify and define project metrics, outcomes, and narratives to support project sustainability including information about the history of over paving, its impacts on the community, and the importance of depaving and tree canopy development.Complete and submit all necessary paperwork and reports in a timely manner; attend and complete all training and service requirements; wear Confluence uniform and/or appropriate identifiers and required safety gear while performing service or attending official events.Abide by program and AmeriCorps policies. Under no circumstances will AmeriCorps Volunteers be asked to perform prohibited activities outlined in the approved grant. Position RequirementsDeep interest in environmental justice, urban forestry, and environmental work.Comfortable engaging directly with private landowners and community members from a wide range of backgrounds; lived experience in community organizing or outreach is valued equally with formal education.Written and verbal communication skills to draft outreach materials, meeting notes, and grant application materials (specific grant-writing experience is not required but is a benefit).Regular and reliable attendance and dependability; ability to serve as part of a team spanning two host organizations.Willingness/openness to learn about and discuss racial equity and social justice issues.Regular and reliable attendance and dependability. AmeriCorps Volunteers must be: 17 years of age or older at beginning of service term; U.S. citizen, national or lawful permanent resident; in possession of a high school diploma or equivalent, or commit to earning one prior to receiving education award; able to commit to the full term of service; able to successfully pass a fingerprint criminal history background check and satisfactory report from the National Sex Offender Public Website (NSOPW) prior to the start of the position.Ability to serve as part of a diverse team. Preferred QualificationsBilingual or multilingual skills relevant to 82nd Avenue's communities (e.g., Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese).Experience or coursework in urban forestry, landscape design, environmental science, or a related field.Familiarity with East Portland or the 82nd Avenue corridor.Experience with data tracking tools (Excel, Google Sheets) or basic GIS/mapping.Experience organizing or facilitating community events or volunteer work. Member Benefits Include$15,200 living allowance paid over the 8-month term of service (approx. $1,688 monthly, before taxes). $5,176 education award (qualified student loans and/or education expenses) Loan Forbearance Health Care InsuranceChild Care Reimbursement Option$50 Training Fund Professional Leadership Certificate, Trainings and Networking opportunities. May be eligible for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).Monthly TriMet passes available.Access to a Member Assistance Program (free counseling, health & financial tips, etc.)Access to a large network of partner organizationsAccess to events, networking, professional development, and conferencesThe knowledge that you’re working on important environmental justice issues facing tens of thousands of folks in east Portland Project Location & Transportation InformationMember’s office space will be at Depave's Portland office located at River Street Studios (820 N River St, Portland OR) in Portland's inner east side. In person organizing/canvassing and site visits will largely occur on/near 82nd Avenue.Portland has a robust public transit network between the office space and 82nd Avenue. The member is encouraged to utilize public transportation and bicycle transportation. Trimet but and Max routes can be found here.

jobs.description: Employer: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture Expires: 10/09/2026 NOTE: Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be considered.Interpretative Research and Programs InternshipHybrid Part-Time Internship and Hybrid Full-Time Internship$425/week and $850/weekJanuary 25 – April 23, 2027Desired Majors and Areas of Study: Museum Studies, Museum Education, African American Studies, Africana/African Diaspora Studies and History, Latin American and Caribbean History, American Studies, Public History, Performance Studies; All encouraged to applyThe Office of Strategic Partnerships (OSP) exists to strengthen the capabilities and sustainability of historical, cultural, and art institutions focused on African American and African Diaspora, which we do through our collaborations with museum service organizations, professional associations, and related organizations.Through collaboration and partnerships, OSP:• Delivers far-reaching and transformative support for under-resourced organizations on a regional, national, and international level;• Connects and builds awareness about the work of its participating institutions;• Provides access to training and resources that support and advance leaders and field-wide best practices.The Interpretative Research and Programs Intern will support the continued development and relaunch of the Ethical Interpretation Workshop, a signature program of the National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC)/OSP. While ethical interpretation is embedded throughout the Museum’s collections, digital platforms, and exhibitions, no single exhibition exclusively focuses on this topic. This internship will play a key role in advancing both a Smithsonian-wide pilot program and a national workshop dedicated to ethical theory and practice, with particular emphasis on illustrating the historical and contemporary relationships between African American communities and the natural world.The selected intern will contribute to the planning, coordination, and preparation of materials for these initiatives, with primary responsibilities centered on research and administrative support. As time permits, the intern may also assist in organizing and facilitating virtual or in-person professional development programs and meetups for the growing Community of Practice focused on ethical interpretation. The intern will join the planning teams for these efforts and support the development of program-related resources and communications.The project will enable the intern to:Gain hands-on experience in planning, coordinating, and developing program materials for the Smithsonian-wide pilot program and national Ethical Interpretation Workshop;Develop a deep understanding of ethical interpretation theory and practice, particularly as it relates to African American and African Diasporic communities and their relationships with the natural world;Conduct object-specific and biographical research to support workshops, and program development;Build skills in interpreting material culture and historical narratives in ways that are accessible and meaningful to a broad, diverse audience, particularly those interested in African American art, history, and culture;Learn to distill large quantities of multimedia exhibition content into thematic, succinct, and engaging museum tours;Gain insight into exhibition rotation cycles, object display length, and the multidisciplinary nature of museum exhibitions and interpretation;Develop object interpretation, public speaking, storytelling, and audience engagement skills;Meet one-on-one with professionals across the museum and broader cultural sector to explore career paths, professional development, and sector-specific opportunities.Through this internship, the intern will gain exposure to the external-facing work of OSP; the national landscape of interpretive practice; models for presenting sensitive historical content; the relationship between interpretation and tourism; and strategies for partnership development, strategic planning, and problem solving. The experience may include site visits to African American museums, universities, and sites of memory throughout the Washington, D.C. metro area, as well as travel to the Association of African American Museums Annual Conference.The ideal candidate will have some knowledge/appreciation for African American History and Public History, experience with partnership development/outreach, and research, and excellent writing and communication skills.Internship Duties Include (but are not limited to):Participate in an online review and physical walkthrough of all museum exhibition galleries with OSP Staff, and other NMAAHC curators, as availableResearch effective methods of program facilitation and audience engagement techniquesIdentify and research key objects on view in NMAAHC exhibitions that fit within the scope and intended content of this projectDevelop a Smithsonian wide exhibition guide centered around ethical interpretation specifically focusing on the narratives of Africans/African AmericansCreate a presentation and/or talking points for each exhibition guide that can be used by other NMAAHC curators, docents, and museum staff on OSP-centered toursUnderstand how to effectively use multiple interpretative methodologies to create impactful public programs, utilizing audience engagement techniquesObserve Museum leadership and strategic planning initiativesAttend virtual cross-departmental meetings, workshops, and special events

jobs.title: Undergraduate Music and Performing Arts Curatorial Internship at Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture
jobs.description: Employer: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture Expires: 10/09/2026 NOTE: Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be considered.Undergraduate Music and Performing Arts Curatorial InternshipPart-Time Hybrid Internship$425/weekJanuary 25 – April 23, 2027Desired Majors and Areas of Study: Museum Studies, Music, Film, Television, Theater History and/or Performance Studies, American historyThis internship is an opportunity to do meaningful curatorial work at one of the most prominent cultural institutions in the country building skills in African American collecting and cultural preservation while expanding professional networks. As part of NMAAHC’s commitment to strengthening the museum talent pipeline, this position is designed to support undergraduate students in gaining foundational knowledge and hands-on experience, while introducing them to the many different career paths that curatorial work can open. The skills developed through this internship (research, writing, object documentation, and professional communication) directly support careers across a wide range of museum positions, including curatorial, collections, education, public programs, and outreach, as well as related fields such as archival work, cultural policy, and the broader nonprofit and public humanities sectors. By the end of the internship the intern will be able to: Navigate and use the TMS (The Museum System) collection information database to locate and support documentation of collection records;Assist with the handling and processing of objects and archival materials following professional conservation and preservation standards;Assist with the creation and review of collection inventories, contributing to the Museum’s collections stewardship goals;Support object research and assist with producing accurate collection documentation as directed by the curator;Research and prepare donor briefs and profiles that support the curator’s donor cultivation and community stewardship efforts;Assist with drafting and editing collection and exhibition texts;Assist with drafting object acquisition proposals using curatorial criteria and an understanding of the museum’s collecting priorities;Produce interpretive labels and an exhibition narrative for a proposed exhibition drawn from the NMAAHC Music & Performing Arts Collection, with support from the curator;Research and write an acquisition proposal with curatorial guidance and present it to the NMAAHC Collections Committee; Develop an understanding of museums as institutions of cultural stewardship and gain insight into the importance of collecting and preservation through direct engagement with the collection and curatorial practice.The Office of Curatorial Affairs advances NMAAHC’s mission of sharing the history and culture of African Americans and all people of African descent with a diverse public by collecting, preserving, researching, and interpreting artifacts of lasting cultural significance. The Music and Performing Arts Curator contributes to this mission by stewarding a collection that spans the full breadth of African American creative expression (including music, television, film, theater, dance, comedy, and popular culture) from everyday creative life to landmark performances, recordings, and cultural movements. All of these areas are available to the intern. As an undergraduate intern, you will assist the curator with collections acquisition and processing, object documentation, research, and writing, supporting an active list of ongoing projects throughout the internship. Before your start date, you will be given a list of Music and Performing Arts collections to select which collection(s) you want to focus on, allowing you to align the experience with your academic interests and professional goals. This internship will strengthen your research and writing skills, expand your professional network across the museum, and give you a clearer sense of the many directions a career in curatorial work can take.This is a hybrid internship, combining remote work with scheduled onsite days at NMAAHC in Washington, DC, and a storage facility in Maryland. Start and end dates are to be determined in coordination with the intern and supervisor.The ideal candidate is an undergraduate student or recent graduate with coursework or a demonstrated interest in African American history and culture, with a focus on music, performing arts, popular culture, or museum studies. A genuine curiosity about Black history and culture and its relationship to music and the performing arts is essential. An interest in developing research and writing skills in a museum setting is important. Prior experience with curatorial or archival work is a plus but not required. Comfort with word processing and spreadsheet software is expected; experience with collection management systems is welcome but not necessary.The internship includes two projects developed with curatorial guidance:The first is a proposed exhibition of your choice drawn from the NMAAHC Music & Performing Arts Collection. With support from the curator, you will select objects and images, conduct research, develop an exhibition narrative, and write interpretive labels resulting in a portfolio piece and writing sample that reflects the full arc of your internship experience.The second is an acquisition proposal. With guidance from the curator, you will research and write a proposal for an object or collection of your choice (which may include contemporary materials that document living artists, emerging genres, or current cultural events) and present it to the NMAAHC Collections Committee.Duties Include (but are not limited to):Attend curatorial team meetings to observe institutional processes and build familiarity with museum operationsDevelop familiarity with the TMS (The Museum System) collection information database to locate documentation of collection recordsAssist with the handling and documentation of objects and archival materials following professional conservation and preservation standardsAssist with the creation and review of collection inventoriesSupport object research and assist with producing accurate collection documentation as directed by the curatorResearch and prepare briefs and profiles for the curator’s visits with potential donorsAssist with drafting and editing collection and exhibition textsAssist with drafting object acquisition proposals in support of ongoing collections workWrite interpretive labels and supporting materials for the exhibition projectResearch and write an acquisition proposal with curatorial guidance and present it to the NMAAHC Collections Committee

jobs.title: Council Oral History Project Internship at Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture
jobs.description: Employer: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture Expires: 10/09/2026 NOTE: Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be considered.Council Oral History Project InternshipHybrid Part-Time Internship$425/weekJanuary 25 – April 19, 2027Desired Majors and Areas of Study: Oral History, Public History, Library Science, Archival Management, Museum Studies, Arts Management, African American History and Cultural Studies, Cultural Heritage and Preservation, Digital Preservation and Records Management, Museum Collections and Collections Management, Nonprofit Leadership and Philanthropy Studies, Archival Research and Information ManagementThe Office of the Director is responsible for guiding the museum’s operation and mission. In coordination with the NMAAHC staff and Council, the Office of the Director oversees the preservation, documentation, display, and dissemination of African American history and culture to a diverse and global audience. The Council Oral History Project Internship provides hands-on experience supporting the preservation and documentation of the history of the National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC). The internship is a collaborative opportunity between the Office of the Director's Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team and the Oral History Initiative within the Office of Digital Strategies and Engagement. The project focuses on collecting, preserving, and organizing the oral histories of Founding Council members who played a significant role in the creation and development of the museum. This internship is designed to provide hands-on experience in oral history, archival preservation, museum operations, and board relations while developing professional communication, research, and project management skills. Through participation in the Council Oral History Project, the intern will gain practical experience supporting the collection, preservation, and interpretation of historical narratives within a museum setting. The intern will develop a greater understanding of how culturally specific museums operate and how oral history programs support exhibitions, research, collections, and public engagement. Through direct involvement with the Oral History Initiative and Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team, the intern will learn how oral history projects are planned, managed, and implemented from concept through accession into a museum collection.As part of the project, the intern will gain professional experience in archival and oral history practices while supporting the preparation and management of oral history interviews and records. Responsibilities may include archiving Council meeting materials, conducting background research on interview subjects, collecting and organizing oral history documentation, reviewing and proofreading transcripts, writing interview summaries and field notes, preparing collections documentation, observing oral history interviews, and assisting with the planning and implementation of public programs. Key learning objectives include:Developing oral history research and documentation skills through conducting background research, gathering metadata, maintaining records, and supporting interview preparation; Learning archival and digital preservation practices, including transcript review, file management, documentation collection, and preservation workflows; Building professional writing and communication skills by preparing interview summaries, field notes, collections justifications, and other project documentation; Gaining an understanding of board and donor relations through exposure to the museum’s Advisory Council and the Founding Council Oral History Project; Learning ethical standards and best practices in oral history collection as established by the Oral History Association;Developing knowledge of museum collections management and the process of bringing materials into a museum collection;Observing and participating in oral history interviews, including interview preparation, documentation, and post-interview processing;Understanding how oral history content is integrated into museum exhibitions, public programs, and educational initiatives.The internship provides hands-on opportunities through active participation in staff meetings, informational interviews with Smithsonian staff and leadership, oral history documentation, transcript processing, archival research, and public programming support. These experiences allow the intern to apply classroom knowledge in a professional museum environment while developing transferable skills in research, project coordination, records management, writing, digital preservation, and stakeholder engagement. These competencies are highly valuable within the museum field and are also transferable to careers in archives, libraries, public history, cultural heritage organizations, nonprofit management, research institutions, education, communications, and project management. The internship equips participants with both specialized museum knowledge and broadly applicable professional skills that support success across a wide range of industries.This project is important because it preserves the firsthand accounts of the leaders whose vision, advocacy, fundraising efforts, and strategic guidance helped establish NMAAHC. Their experiences provide unique insight into the museum’s creation, from the early efforts to establish the museum through site selection, fundraising, and the museum’s opening. By documenting and preserving these stories, the project ensures that an important part of the museum’s institutional history is available to future researchers, museum professionals, and the public. The internship directly supports the work of both the Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team and the Oral History Initiative. The Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team is responsible for managing the museum’s Advisory Council and advancing museum-wide initiatives, while the Oral History Initiative works to document, preserve, and interpret African American stories through oral history projects that support research, exhibitions, programming, and public engagement. The project aligns closely with NMAAHC’s mission by contributing to the preservation, documentation, and dissemination of African American history and culture. Through oral history collection, archival preservation, and public access initiatives, the project helps ensure that the stories of individuals who shaped the museum and contributed to its success are preserved and shared with diverse audiences for generations to come.The ideal candidate will have a strong interest in oral history, historical research, archives, museum operations, and the preservation and interpretation of African American history and culture. The internship is particularly valuable for students seeking careers in museums, archives, libraries, cultural institutions, public history organizations, and related nonprofit or educational sectors. Preferred qualifications include:Demonstrated interest in oral history interviews and oral history methodology;Interest in African American history, cultural studies, the history of philanthropy, and culturally specific museum leadership; Interest in systems thinking, workflows, and process improvement; Strong organizational skills and attention to detail;Ability to work independently and manage self-directed assignments;Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively both independently and in collaborative team environments.Desired technical and professional competencies include experience or interest in conducting research, reviewing and proofreading written materials, maintaining records and documentation, managing digital files, and supporting archival or oral history projects. Familiarity with Microsoft Office applications, digital collaboration tools, and database or records management systems is beneficial but not required. The selected intern will support the Council Oral History Project through a combination of daily responsibilities, short-term assignments, and long-term projects that provide practical experience in oral history, archival preservation, museum operations, and research. These duties are designed to help the intern achieve the learning objectives of the internship while contributing to the preservation of NMAAHC's institutional history. These responsibilities provide the intern with progressive, hands-on experience in oral history methodology, archival management, research, professional writing, digital preservation, and museum operations while contributing to a project that preserves the stories of the leaders who helped shape the National Museum of African American History and Culture.Internship Duties Include (but are not limited to):Attend staff meetings and mandatory training sessionsParticipate in informational interviews with Smithsonian staff and museum leadershipConduct background research on interview subjects and topics related to oral history projectsCollect, organize, and maintain oral history documentation and project records Review, reformat, proofread, and process oral history transcripts Write interview summaries, field notes, and supporting project documentation Observe oral history interviews and assist with interview preparation and follow-up activitiesSupport the planning and implementation of public programs related to oral history initiativesSupport the archiving and organization of historical Council meeting records for the Council Oral History Project Assist in documenting and preserving oral histories of Council members and other project participants Prepare and compile background research materials that support oral history interviews and project development Assist with metadata collection, records management, and digital preservation activities associated with oral history collections. Draft justifications and supporting documentation for collections-related review processesContribute to ongoing oral history project workflows from interview planning and documentation through transcript processing and archival preparationSupport efforts to make oral history materials accessible for future research, exhibitions, programming, and public engagement

Work designationThis position is fully remote. All core responsibilities are performed independently and do not require a fixed on-site schedule.The team looks for opportunities to meet in person when project timelines and individual schedules align. These gatherings are intentional but informal, driven by shared momentum rather than a fixed cadence. Skipper AI core valuesTrust and Transparency. We communicate openly, follow through on commitments, and treat every client and colleague with honesty. Trust is the foundation of every relationship we build. Humble Hunger. There's more to a failed task than the task itself; every mistake carries a lesson, and progress in anything is still progress forward. It's okay to be wrong, as long as you admit it. What matters is being hungry more often than you are wrong. Have Hard Conversations. One's success in life is directly correlated to their ability to have hard conversations. Conversations are hard if you are passionate, and two passionate people in a room is a rare thing. About Skipper AIIn the last year, we have worked with 8 companies, on countless projects, and have shipped things that did and didn't work. Importantly, we have captured the themes behind what leads to success or failure, and have not found a use case since those learnings did not apply. Skipper AI exists to not skip them. We've driven 90%+ adoption not because of the platform we picked, but because we refuse to skip the intentional steps. Intentionality through change has never been more important. The tools are the easy part; it's the steps most firms rush past, the change management in between where AI actually sticks or quietly dies.

Expires: 10/10/2026 Project Management InternPosition SummaryThe Project Management Intern supports the safe, efficient, and profitable delivery of electrical construction projects while learning how work moves from estimate and preconstruction through field execution, billing, closeout, and customer follow-up. Working alongside Project Managers, project support team members, field leaders, Estimating, VDC, Prefabrication, Safety, and other partners, the intern assists with project documentation, planning, coordination, material and vendor follow-up, cost awareness, and communication. jobs.description: Employer: Clark Construction Group Expires: 10/10/2026 At Clark, we build leaders—individuals who take ownership, rise to challenges, and deliver the Clark standard of excellence. Across the industry, Clark is known for exceptional performance and shaping communities through some of the most complex, high-profile projects being built today.We empower you to take on significant responsibility early, backing your growth with extensive resources, mentorship, formal training, and a culture that challenges you to advance your career further. Here, the standard is higher. Our team doesn't just build landmark projects—we build the leaders who make them possible. The RoleThe Summer Associate Program is your opportunity to build a comprehensive understanding of the construction industry and our business. As a summer associate, you will be fully embedded with a team on a jobsite or in a department, gaining hands-on experience across project management, field management, project development, and business operations. Beyond your project work, you will become an integrated member of the Clark community through training and development opportunities. Build your network through social events and jobsite tours, and sharpen your skills with formal training sessions led by Clark experts. Other cornerstones of the Summer Associate Program include: The Capstone Project: A team-based project that challenges you to develop innovative solutions for real-time business opportunities. You will present your findings directly to company leadership, gaining visibility and the chance to make a tangible impact.The Passport Experience: A curated series of experiences designed to guide your summer journey. The Passport showcases the full breadth of Clark’s business, helps you establish meaningful connections across the company, and ensures you gain essential industry knowledge. This immersive, full-time program runs for 8 -10 weeks and begins in late May or early June. Responsibilities Throughout the summer, you will be exposed to:Project Management: Working in project management gives you an understanding of the day-to-day and long-term business and financial management associated with construction projects.Financial Management - Review gross billings, track change orders, and subcontractor requisitions Document Control - Manage the submittals, RFI, and material tracking process Trade Partner Success - Become a trusted advisor to our subcontractors to plan for a successful field installationField Management: Learn the intricacies of the building process, assist in site logistics, and ensure quality and safety on our jobsites.Quality Control and Safety - Monitor tradeworkers with emphasis on the quality of work and safetyProject Schedule - Assist with schedule management and site logistics Critical Thinking - Resolve unforeseen challenges within installation, schedule, and trade partner coordinationProject Development: Understand how we acquire new work, develop winning strategies, and build strong client relationships through budgeting, estimating, and purchasingBudgeting - Review initial contract documents, solicit, and provide preliminary evaluations of subcontractor bidsEstimating - Perform quantity takeoffs, prepare the overall bid proposal, and quantify labor and material prices required for projects Purchasing - Collaborate to execute subcontractor agreements, review the scope of work, and manage relationships with subcontractorsBusiness Operations: Explore the essential functions that keep our company running smoothly, gaining a holistic view of the Clark organization. Basic QualificationsPursuing an undergraduate degree or equivalent, or a graduate degreeInterest and passion for the construction industry What a Successful Candidate Looks LikeWe look for individuals who embody these core principles:Enthusiasm & Drive: Be punctual and dedicated, staying until work is done. Arrive early for meetings and events. Be a proactive team player – ask how you can help and be present. Take initiative, represent the company professionally (dress, demeanor), and build trust with your team, clients, and stakeholders. Proactively seek ways to contribute to team success, and always maintain a positive attitude.Delivery & Performance: Reliably meet the expectations of your role and commitments. Understand and follow Clark's standard procedures. Take on new responsibilities, dig into the details, and bring solutions to problems. Take ownership, be accountable, and demonstrate responsiveness with a sense of urgency.Learning & Growth: Immerse yourself in Clark's culture, your team, and your community. Fulfill Clark Corporate University learning requirements. Be engaged, accountable, and self-directed in your learning – be curious! Continuously build your technical expertise and grow your business acumen. The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings.Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines.A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment fitness for duty screening is required, and random fitness for duty tests of employees are conducted quarterly.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Graphic Design Intern at Marketing for Change
jobs.description: Employer: Marketing for Change Expires: 10/11/2026 The Change Academy at Marketing for Change offers graduate students, college seniors, recent graduates and other emerging creatives a paid semester-long experience working and learning at one of the nation’s leading behavior-change marketing agencies. In behavior-change marketing, the objective is not sales or profits; it’s influencing behaviors in a way that leads to a healthier, safer, more sustainable world. We’re looking for a Graphic Design & Creative Intern who wants to put their creative skills to work on real projects with real impact. You’ll work alongside our creative team and other experts across the agency, gaining hands-on experience developing visual concepts and creative work for campaigns designed to make a difference. As part of the Change Academy, you’ll have opportunities to contribute to real client work while strengthening your design skills and learning how behavioral science informs creative strategy. Depending on the project, your work may include graphic design, visual concepting, campaign creative, digital and social content, presentation design, and other visual storytelling. You’ll receive mentorship and skill-specific training from experienced creatives, along with broader training in behavioral science and behavior-change marketing. You’ll also participate in agency events, client meetings and, if you want, off-the-clock social gatherings. Interns earn $18.40 an hour or minimum wage (whichever is higher) and work 20 hours a week, with at least one day a week in our offices. The in-office experience is critical to helping interns improve their skills, work directly with mentors and share a group experience with their cohort. Please confirm you can participate in person at your selected location. LocationOur work hubs are located in Orlando and just outside Washington, DC, and we very much prefer to hire people willing to locate in those areas. We are mostly a hybrid workforce with staff working together in-person at least one day a week because we value the fun and collaboration that allows. The program lasts between 12 and 16 weeks depending on the semester. Instruction takes place during the first 6 to 8 weeks of the internship, mixed with group projects and real work experience. The final weeks focus on work experience and give interns an opportunity to build their portfolios with meaningful, professional creative experience. The Change Academy is the main path to entry-level employment at Marketing for Change. Several former M4C interns are now in leadership roles at M4C, including an art director, creative director, senior media planner and strategist. What we’re looking for:Relevant experience, coursework or training in graphic design, visual communication, advertising, art direction or a related creative field. Preference is given to graduate students, recent graduates or college seniors with at least one prior internship or comparable creative experience. Other adults with the right skills but no degree may also apply. Several have been successful in the past.A portfolio or work samples that show your design skills, creative thinking and visual point of view. School, internship, freelance and personal projects are all welcome.Familiarity with common design tools and an interest in continuing to build your creative and technical skills.A willingness to take feedback, try new ideas and collaborate with other creatives, strategists and agency teams.Deep curiosity about what makes people tick and how design can influence what people notice, feel and do.An interest in using your creative powers for good and making the world a better place.Being a nice person. Seriously. We want the kind of person most other people love to work with. A quick note about our hiring processApplying for a job can feel a little like sending your application out into the void and hoping a real person is on the other side. At Marketing for Change, one will be. Real people on our team review every application. We may use technology to make parts of the process easier, but when it comes to getting to know you, considering what you could bring to our team and making hiring decisions, that’s us. We know there’s a real person on the other side of every application, too. Someone who gave us their time, shared a little bit of their story and decided we might be worth exploring. We don’t take that lightly. And if you’re considering us, we’re genuinely glad you’re here. Note: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification. TimingSeptember 2026 to January 2027

jobs.title: Communications and Marketing Intern at Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit
jobs.description: Employer: Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit Expires: 10/11/2026 The Communications and Marketing Intern under general supervision, provides administrative and technical assistance in support of SMART’s community outreach and education efforts, employee communications, and marketing campaigns, including writing and editing material for publication, assisting with the details of projects such as the production and handling of project information, distribution of printed materials, logistics for public meetings and outreach events, and other associated tasks; attends public outreach events; adheres to set schedules to keep projects moving to meet deadlines; work will include assisting in the preparation of documents and website content that summarize the District’s service, fares and schedules as well as plans and activities for the continued construction of the SMART rail and bicycle/pedestrian project.Examples of DutiesPosition duties and skills include, but are not limited to, the following:Assists SMART Communications and Marketing Staff in coordinating public meetings, creating and coordinating informational publications, placing advertisements in local publications, and making reservations.Staff informational booths at summer fairs and festivals for the SMART Communications department, which includes set-up, clean-up, contacting organizations, serving as the SMART point of contact, creating associated materials, attending the event as a SMART representative and responding to project related questions.Assists in the logistics of materials and AV equipment for meetingsActs as a liaison and coordinates with the Communications and Marketing Staff regarding events, informational materials, advertisements, and displays;Assists in the preparation of agendas and presentation materials for community outreach meetings, special events and public hearings.Assists in preparing outreach materials as directed by senior department staff as required in a timely manner.May assist with developing and maintaining website and social media content.Must be able to participate in meetings and outreach activities on weekends and evenings;Performs related work as required. Minimum QualificationsExperience and Education:Sufficient training, education and experience to demonstrate the required knowledge skills and abilities. Typically, coursework in public relations, planning, journalism, marketing, communications or a related field. Possession of a valid California driver’s license is required at the time of appointment. Knowledge of:Principles, methods and techniques of effective public communications, public relations, news media communications and community outreach;Principles and techniques of preparing advertising, writing copy, layout and production.Standard English usage, spelling, grammar and punctuation.Techniques for making effective presentations to individuals and groups.Techniques for effectively dealing with the media.Techniques for preparing effective written and audio-visual materials. Desired SkillsSpanish speaking a plusProficiency in Microsoft Office and Adobe Creative SuiteCopywritingProficiency in various Social Media platformsExperience with public speaking, presenting and interfacing with the public Ability to:Organize, establish priorities, and set goals and objectives.Identify and define technical problems.Compile and analyze data from a variety of sources;Communicate ideas and concepts through creative writing and presentations to large and small groups;Make effective presentations to individuals and groups of varying ages, interests and backgrounds.Draft, edit and proofread written materials for publication;Plan and organize outreach and promotional activities;Use sound independent judgment within general policy and procedural guidelines.Complete multiple assignments efficiently and meet established deadlines in a fast paced team environment;Prepare clear and accurate reports, correspondence and other written materials.Operate a personal computer with common software applications; learn specialty software of the work unit;Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of the work.Communicate effectively both verbally and in written form.Work collaboratively with other divisions and co-workers.Maintain accurate records and files.Work non-traditional hours, including weekends, holidays and evenings. Physical Working Conditions:Position requires ability to remain in a stationary position for prolonged periods in the performance of daily activities. Occasionally requires the ability to move over uneven terrain and to work outdoors in all types of weather when working at community events. The position also requires ability to perform data entry and to prepare reports using a computer keyboard. Additionally, the position requires ability to read written reports and work-related documents. Requires ability to provide phone and personal service. The need to lift, drag, and push files, boxes, equipment, paper and documents weighing up to 50 pounds is also required. The ability to use a personal computer and the ability to speak clearly and concisely to obtain and relay information are required. Ability to travel to SMART office locations and to community events and meetings is required. Most work is performed in an office environment. May occasionally be exposed to extreme weather conditions and noise when working at events. Some of these requirements may be accommodated for otherwise qualified individuals requiring and requesting such accommodations. Position Details:Salary Range: $20.00 per hourFLSA Status: Non-exemptThis position is part-time, at-will, temporaryThis position is not eligible for benefitsSMART is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Brand Content Intern at Solvely.ai
jobs.description: Employer: Solvely.ai Expires: 10/11/2026 Type: Internship · Part-Time · RemoteLocation: United StatesDescriptionKickstart your content marketing career with Solvely!Solvely is an AI-powered academic tool that helps college students solve complex problems across STEM, business, and more. The students we build for are also the people who know our product best, which is why we hire student creators to make content that actually speaks to other students.We're looking for Brand Content Interns to join our marketing team and create short-form video content (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts) about how students study, learn, and use AI tools in their academic lives. You'll be part of a structured 10–12 week internship: we provide weekly scripts and content themes, plus mentorship from our marketing team.You’ll be a fit if you’re:Comfortable being on camera and speaking naturallyConsistent and reliable, able to commit to a weekly content scheduleInterested in social media marketing, content creation, or short-form videoFamiliar with TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube ShortsWhy Solvely:Hands-on mentorship in short-form content marketing.A real, build-able portfolio.** Every video, account, and performance dashboard you produce is yours to keep. By the end of the internship, you'll have a body of work that proves you can ship content at scale.Interns who consistently exceed performance benchmarks are eligible for a recommendation letter from Solvely.Use our AI study tool for your own coursework for free throughout the internship.RequirementsCurrently enrolled US-based college studentStrong English communication skillsInterest in AI-assisted learning and how students use AI tools in their academic lifeBasic short-form video editing skills (CapCut, InShot, Premiere, or similar)ResponsibilitiesManage your dedicated brand account on TikTok, Instagram Reels, and/or YouTube ShortsTrack basic content performance and share weekly observations with our marketing teamProduce 5 short-form videos per week following our weekly scripts and filming templatesMaintain a consistent posting cadence and iterate based on what's workingApplySubmit your application: In addition to the required written information, please share a previous explainer-style short video you've made — could be from school projects, club content, or personal social media. If you don't have one on hand, you could also try filming a quick 20–30 second talking-head clip sharing something about your student life (study tips, campus moments, a course experience, etc.).Application screening — we review your resume, sample video and short answers, and respond within 3 business days.Onboarding — selected interns receive a contract, onboarding guide, and the first week's content templates. We onboard on a rolling basis throughout Fall 2026.

jobs.title: Loss Prevention Intern at Agropur
jobs.description: Employer: Agropur Expires: 10/12/2026 People are at the heart of our success. Our culture encourages collaboration, transparency, and accountability to create value and achieve sustainable results. Being part of Agropur means joining a team where your contributions matter, your ideas are heard, and your work has a meaningful impact on the future of our business. At Agropur, every role is designed to create value and drive results. As an Loss Prevention Intern, you will work alongside the Safety Manager and other members of the Plant Leadership team on various tasks and projects to help ensure plant compliance with all rules/regulations and gain firsthand experience in a world-class dairy manufacturing environment. Why Choose Agropur?As an Loss Prevention Intern, you'll gain more than just internship experience. You'll have the opportunity to:Earn competitive payReceive relocation assistance (where applicable)Lead and contribute to meaningful, business-impacting projectsGain real-world in in loss prevention, risk management, and workplace security experienceBuild relationships with plant leaders and industry professionalsExpand your professional network across a leading dairy cooperativeExplore future career opportunities within Agropur Where You Will Drive ValueSupport safety initiatives and continuous improvement projects that enhance employee health, safety, and operational performance.Assist with safety program evaluations, including Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), Confined Space, and Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) programs.Collect, analyze, and track data to measure the effectiveness of implemented safety improvements.Support incident and near-miss investigations and help identify corrective and preventive actions.Assist in developing, updating, and communicating safety procedures, training materials, and employee resources.Partner with employees and leaders across the plant to identify hazards, improve safety awareness, and promote a strong safety culture.Gain exposure to regulatory requirements, industry best practices, and environmental health and safety programs.Present project outcomes, recommendations, and key learnings at the conclusion of the internship. What Will Enable You to Have an ImpactCurrently pursuing an Associate's, Bachelor's, or Master's degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Health & Safety, Engineering, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Science, or a related field.Strong attention to detail and commitment to workplace safety.Effective verbal and written communication skills.Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.Interest in safety management systems, risk assessment, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement. Join a Team Where Your Impact MattersAt Agropur, interns are treated as valuable contributors, not observers. You'll gain hands-on experience, develop professional skills, and contribute to projects that create real business value while helping produce high-quality dairy products enjoyed by consumers every day.

This internship offers hands-on experience in event sales, marketing, and operations at one of the world's most iconic venues. jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Public Relations Intern at The Neibart Group
jobs.description: Employer: The Neibart Group Expires: 10/12/2026 JOIN THE NEIBART GROUP TEAMStart your communications career as an intern at The Neibart Group (TNG). This is generally a 3-month internship but could be extended or could lead to fulltime employment. One of the core benefits of working at TNG is the high-touch, hands-on experience you’ll have from the start. We’re eager to see you advance and to provide opportunities to shine. Your contributions will shape how far and fast you progress. TNG is a boutique, full-service corporate communications agency specializing in the financial and professional services sectors. Headquartered in DUMBO, Brooklyn—“the creative capital of New York City”—we bring the client roster of a large agency and the spirit of a small business.Day in the Life of an TNG INTERN: While no two days are the same, here’s a sample of what could end up on your to-do list. Account Coordination: Day-to-day client deliverables; contribute proactive ideas; manage deliverables to keep us on track, deliver great client serviceMedia Intelligence: Conduct research to identify timely news, trends and target journalists; evaluate client-generated content for potential media opportunities; provide analyses to support client objectives and inform communication strategiesMedia Monitoring: Monitor media for client coverage and industry trends; compile reporting metrics; manage media databaseWriting: Draft frameworks for press releases and articles; write social copy and web content; prepare media pitches and compose reporter briefing documentsWho is our ideal candidate? Someone who is genuinely excited about joining our team, contributing to our company culture, and telling the story of our clients. We’re also looking for candidates with:A bachelor’s degree (it’s a plus if it’s in communications and/or business)Someone who has graduated college, or will soon, and has other internship experienceSomeone who is a self-starter, creative, and eager to learnSomeone interested in the world of business and financePlease note: We are not a marketing agency. If you are looking for a marketing job, we are not the best fit. So, what’s next? Does TNG sound like the right fit for you? Drop us a line and attach your CV. We’d love to chat.ApplicationsWhen submitting your resumé, please include a cover note of no more than 250 words outlining why you would like to join our specific firm. We look forward to learning more about you!Company Website | LinkedIn | Instagram

We're WebFX, a full-service digital marketing agency based in the US. We've been 10x named the Best Place To Work in Pennsylvania, and we'd love to meet you! We are a fast-growing company that has doubled in size over the past 5 years, with talented team members now based around the globe (and representing 18+ different countries!). While we are growing at a rapid rate, we are committed to growing strategically and sustainably, and that starts with growing our team of the #BestCoworkers - that’s where you come in!We're looking for people to join our mission to provide world-class digital marketing solutions to mid-size businesses around the world. We are passionate about what we do, we’re committed to driving business growth for our clients, and we’re on the hunt for people just like you, who take pride in their work and want to be part of a company that does too.Why Choose WebFX?Vibrant Company Culture: We've been named the Best Place To Work in Pennsylvania 10 times Individual and Company Growth: Merit-based promotions with a clear progression path. WebFX grew 250% over the past 3 years, and we promote almost exclusively internallyTraining and Development: Entry-level roles, comprehensive training, ongoing learning programs, and the chance to learn from some of the best in the businessFlexible Schedule: Start your day between 8-10 am - when you do your best work Insurance Coverage: Health, vision, dental, and supplemental insurance with multiple plans and options to choose from, including HSA and FSA options with contribution matching 100% Company 401k Matching: Up to 4% Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, new parent support (and paw-ternity leave!) Tech and Equipment: All technology & equipment provided - every FXer receives a tech set-up valued at ~$1500, plus a personal desk fund for any extra touches you want to add to your space! Health & Wellness: 24/7 on-site gym and an employee wellness program including a free FitBit, fitness challenges, and a Headspace account Office Perks: Complimentary coffee service by our on-site barista, tea bar, pet-friendly office spaces, casual dress code, surprise catered meals, and more Opportunities to Give Back: On top of charitable donation matching and local volunteer opportunities, our #FXBuilds program has positively impacted over 15,000 people around the world - and every individual FXer's work directly contributes...And So Much More! Home buyer program, profit sharing, personal desk fund, green commute benefits, and the opportunity to be part of a passionate, driven team where we pride ourselves on delivering high-quality work that makes a real-world impact for our clientsCheck out our culture on social media:InstagramTwitterFacebook*You don't need to apply more than once even if you're interested in multiple positions - you can simply let us know! We consider all open roles when reviewing resumes and applications!We have a multi-step interview process, where we focus on giving both our candidates, and ourselves, opportunities to get to know each other a bit better. While our process may be more thorough and perhaps longer than other interview processes that you've been a part of, our goal is to work together with our candidates to find a mutually beneficial fit, where a candidate is a great addition to the FXFamily, and WebFX is the right fit for their career goals. Interested in joining the FXFamily? You should definitely apply now!WebFX is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to providing and fostering an inclusive environment where all people, including women, minorities, LGBTQ+ and other underrepresented groups are supported, respected, and encouraged to excel within STEM careers. Our goal as an organization is to empower our team to achieve their personal best, bring people together, and provide equal opportunity to do so regardless of race, age, gender, sexual orientation, religion, physical ability or disability, or political affiliation. You can learn more on our website here!We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

jobs.description: Employer: The Toro Company Expires: 10/12/2026 The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program.Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future. Who Are We? The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA.Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. We market and sell TTC products worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental center and home centers—as well as online direct to end users.The Commercial marketing team serves to effectively market products designed and manufactured to meet the needs of professional turf managers such as; golf course superintendents, professional sports grounds crews and municipal parks grounds managers. This includes but is not limited to market and sales analysis, event management, and media planning (print, digital, and social media). Additionally, we operate as marketing support for our nationwide distributor network. What Will You Do? We aim to provide a well-rounded internship experience that provides a variety of marketing opportunities. As part of a successful internship with The Toro Company, you may be asked to contribute to: Assisting with ongoing marketing initiatives including product launch efforts and media campaigns. Participating in product photo and video shoots including collaborating with our media production team, helping to procure and manage talent, and coordinating logistics of the shoots. Analyzing market and sales data identify growth opportunities.Support customer event at The Toro Company headquarters and/or local event venues/stadiums.Execute media plan elements that help customers learn about our commercial product line.Work cross-divisionally to support new product development What Do You Need? To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements: Completed your junior year of college with an average GPA of 3.0 or higher.In pursuit of a degree in marketing or a related field (advertising, PR, graphic design, or business.)Have excellent oral and written communication skills.Have working knowledge of the Microsoft365 suite of products including Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Experience with graphic design is preferred.Be team-oriented, an enthusiastic self-starter, curious about the world around you, and passionate about creating impactful marketing. What Can We Give You? At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our interns know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive pay- The Toro Company offers interns a variety of perks, including: Dress for your day – We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment. Volunteerism – The Toro Company is proud to provide interns 8 hours of paid time to volunteer in the community. Summer Hours *Based on Location* – Enjoy a flexible schedule during the summer! By working a little more during the first few days of the week, TTC employees at certain locations are able to start their weekends early and leave by noon on Friday. Competitive Pay – Competitive compensation with an anticipated hourly rate of $20–$24. Actual rates may vary based on factors such as academic standing, business function, and other relevant considerations. The Toro Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. For each example, explain your role and describe any experience with cameras, audio equipment, or livestreaming.

jobs.description: Employer: Bandon Dunes Golf Resort Expires: 10/14/2026 As a Golf Intern at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort, you'll get real hands-on experience at one of the world's top golf destinations while pursuing your Professional Golf Management degree. You'll work directly with guests, manage our golf shop, coordinate tournaments, and learn the business side of golf operations. This isn't just shadowing someone—you'll have actual responsibilities that matter to our guests' experiences on courses that rank among the top 16 public courses in America.About Bandon Dunes Golf Resort:Bandon Dunes is a world-class golf resort located on the Oregon Coast near the charming community of Bandon. Guests come to experience golf as it was meant to be at Bandon Dunes' six distinct golf courses. That includes five 18-hole courses, which all rank among the top 16 public courses in the United States, according to Golf Digest. The resort is also home to an award-winning par-3 course, Bandon Preserve. A second par-3 course, Shorty's, will open in 2024. The two short courses are 'Courses with a Mission,' with all net proceeds funding the Bandon Dunes Charitable Foundation. The Foundation supports communities along the South Coast of Oregon.Beyond premier golf, guests delight in a variety of dining options at Bandon Dunes’ collection of restaurants. Whether you're looking to enjoy locally-sourced, Pacific-Northwest cuisine accompanied by an award-winning wine list, or prefer kicking back in a Scottish-style setting with traditional pub fare and local microbrews, there is something for everyone.Working at Bandon Dunes is a dream for golf fans, outdoor enthusiasts, and hospitality professionals alike. The Bandon Dunes team works together to create trips of a lifetime for our guests. We are passionate stewards of our resort, our community, and our environment. As an endlessly curious group, we ask questions, share ideas, and always look for a better way. With a hard-working attitude, we help guide our guests through their pure golf experience, immersed in Oregon’s natural beauty and away from the demands of daily life.What You'll Do:Learn the retail side of golf. You'll become an expert on our golf shop merchandise, help guests find what they need, and handle special orders. This means understanding products well enough to make real recommendations, not just ringing up sales.Handle real transactions. You'll process merchandise sales, greens fees, and equipment rentals while keeping accurate records. You'll learn the financial side of golf operations through actual daily work, not textbook theory.Provide genuine customer service. You'll answer guest questions, schedule tee times, and maintain professional phone interactions. When guests call, you'll be the voice they hear representing Bandon Dunes.Support tournaments and events. You'll help organize competitions and special events, coordinating between different departments to make sure everything runs smoothly. This is where you'll see how all the moving pieces fit together.Manage inventory and operations. You'll help keep merchandise displays organized, assist with inventory counts, and support various services like handicapping systems and driving range operations.What Makes You a Great Fit:You're pursuing a Professional Golf Management degree. We work with certified PGM programs and prefer students who can commit to a 6-month internship. This gives you enough time to really learn the business, not just get a quick overview.You communicate well. Strong written and verbal skills matter here because you'll interact with guests from around the world. You need to sound professional on the phone and explain complex golf services clearly.You can handle multiple priorities. Golf operations move fast, and you'll need to manage several tasks while staying calm under pressure. If you get flustered easily when things get busy, this probably isn't the right fit.You're flexible with your schedule. Golf doesn't stop for weekends or holidays. You'll work evenings, weekends, and busy periods when our guests need us most.Special Intern Benefits:Shared staff housing available for a reasonable fee, mentorship from industry professionals, and the chance to play golf for free on seven award-winning courses.If you're serious about a career in golf and want to learn the business at one of the world's premier destinations, we'd like to hear from you. This internship will give you real experience you can't get in a classroom, plus the chance to build relationships with industry professionals. You'll work hard, but you'll also get to play some of the best golf of your life on your days off.Ready to embark on an enriching journey in the world of golf? Apply today to become a Golf Intern at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort and be part of a team dedicated to providing one of the world’s most exceptional golfing experiences.At Bandon Dunes Golf Resort, we are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
